newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean gold prices rise ahead of wedding season.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean gold prices rise ahead of wedding season.

text.p: South Korean gold prices rose this week on indications of good demand for the current wedding season, which starts in March, and on higher international prices, dealers in Seoul said on Tuesday.
"In the past week, domestic bullion prices have risen considerably on what looks like good demand ahead of the upcoming wedding season," a dealer with Ssangyong Corp said.

Gold producer LG Metals' daily selling price for the precious metal, which is regarded as a benchmark for the local bullion wholesale market, rose on Tuesday to 10,470 won per gram from 10,200 a week ago.
The company's silver price has also risen by three won a gram to 163 won in the past week.

Some dealers said the domestic bullion market was expected to experience a tightening in supply as major participants hold back metal and also due to reduced smuggling stemming from increased security measures because of inter-Korean tensions.
They said several domestic gold suppliers were seen reducing their sales from early March on expectations of higher prices.
South Korea's current account deficit soared to $3.09 billion in January from a $1.72 billion shortfall a year earlier, preliminary figures from the Bank of Korea showed on Tuesday.
The telegraphic transfer selling rate for customers, posted by the Korea Exchange Bank, rose to 867.00 won against the dollar from 867.80 won a week ago.
The rate is regarded as a benchmark for local foreign exchange rates by domestic companies.
